quests.scene: Your colleague accidentally sends you an email clearly meant for someone else.
options: Share it with the whole team!
Hi I think this was meant for someone else.
Save it for later.
Read it carefully and say nothing.
quests.hint: The polite and honest thing is to let the sender know immediately.
quests.explanation: Telling the sender I think this was meant for someone else is honest and respectful.

quests.scene: In a job interview the interviewer asks: What is your greatest weakness?
options: I have absolutely no weaknesses.
I can sometimes be too hardworking.
I sometimes struggle with time management and I'm actively working on better planning habits.
I'd rather not answer that.
quests.hint: Be genuinely honest but always show self-awareness and a plan to improve.
quests.explanation: Naming a real weakness and explaining what you are doing about it shows self-awareness and a growth mindset.

quests.scene: You accidentally bump into someone and knock their coffee out of their hand.
options: Watch where you're going!
I'm so sorry! Are you all right? Can I get you another one?
That was an accident.
You shouldn't have been standing there.
quests.hint: When you cause an accident take responsibility immediately and offer to help.
quests.explanation: Apologising immediately and offering a replacement shows good character.

quests.scene: Your friend says: I've been feeling really low lately.
options: Just cheer up.
That's tough. Do you want to talk about it?
Everyone feels like that.
You'll be fine.
quests.hint: Show genuine empathy first then offer to listen without judgment.
quests.explanation: That's tough. Do you want to talk about it? validates your friend's feelings without dismissing them.

quests.scene: A street performer finishes their act and looks hopefully at the crowd. You enjoyed it.
options: Ignore them and walk away.
Clap and drop a coin in their hat.
Say nice job and walk on.
Whistle very loudly.
quests.hint: Show appreciation for the performer's talent and effort in the appropriate way.
quests.explanation: Clapping and giving a small tip is the socially appropriate response to enjoying a street performance.

quests.scene: During a meeting someone starts talking at exactly the same time as you.
options: Keep talking as loudly as you can.
Stop and say: Sorry please go ahead.
Ignore them completely.
Say I was speaking first.
quests.hint: Yielding the floor shows social grace and good manners.
quests.explanation: Saying Sorry please go ahead when you accidentally interrupt someone shows excellent manners.

quests.scene: A neighbour knocks on your door late at night to say the noise is disturbing them.
options: Tell them to go away.
I'm so sorry I didn't realise. I'll keep it down straight away.
You can't tell me what to do.
I wasn't being loud at all.
quests.hint: A neighbour's complaint deserves respect and a quick solution.
quests.explanation: Apologising and agreeing to lower the noise is the respectful considerate response.

quests.scene: You overhear a coworker giving a client incorrect information about your product.
options: Tell the client the truth afterward without the coworker present.
Say nothing - it's not your problem.
Politely step in: Excuse me I think I can add something useful here.
Report your coworker to management immediately.
quests.hint: Correct the information without embarrassing your colleague.
quests.explanation: Excuse me I think I can add something here is tactful - it corrects the error while preserving dignity.

quests.scene: You are about to board your flight and cannot find your boarding pass anywhere.
options: Wait quietly and hope it turns up.
Tell the airline staff immediately and explain the situation calmly.
Try to walk through without it.
Go back home.
quests.hint: Act quickly and tell the right people when a travel problem arises.
quests.explanation: Telling the airline staff immediately is the only practical response.

quests.scene: A new employee asks you to explain something you know very well.
options: Do it yourself.
I don't have time to explain everything.
Of course - let me walk you through it step by step.
Ask the manager.
quests.hint: Sharing knowledge generously is a sign of a great team member.
quests.explanation: Offering to explain something step by step shows patience generosity and strong communication skills.

quests.scene: A customer is upset about a long wait. You are the shop assistant.
options: It's not my fault.
I understand the wait has been frustrating. I'll look into this right away.
Come back another day.
Everyone is waiting not just you.
quests.hint: Acknowledge the customer's frustration first then take action.
quests.explanation: Validating the customer's frustration and committing to action is the professional empathetic response.

quests.scene: Your friend is moving house this weekend and asks for your help. You are already busy.
options: I can't help sorry.
I'm not really into that kind of thing.
I'm quite busy this weekend - could I help you with the unpacking during the week instead?
Hire someone.
quests.hint: Offer a genuine alternative rather than giving a flat refusal.
quests.explanation: Offering to help at a different time shows you care while being honest about your availability.

quests.scene: Your boss asks you to take on another project when you are already at full capacity.
options: Sure no problem at all.
No I'm too busy.
I'm currently working on X and Y. Could we discuss priorities before I take this on?
Give it to someone else.
quests.hint: Be honest about your workload without simply refusing.
quests.explanation: Naming your current commitments and asking to discuss priorities is professionally assertive.

quests.scene: Your meal at a restaurant arrives and it is not what you ordered.
options: Eat it to avoid a fuss.
Demand to speak to the manager immediately.
Excuse me I think there's been a mix-up - I ordered the pasta not the risotto.
Say nothing but leave a very bad review later.
quests.hint: Address the mistake directly and politely so it can be fixed.
quests.explanation: Pointing out the error calmly and specifically allows the waiter to correct it without confrontation.

quests.scene: You need to leave a voicemail for a business contact who did not answer.
options: Just hang up.
Say Hi call me back and hang up.
Hi this is [name] calling about our meeting on Friday. Could you call me back at [number]? Thank you.
Leave a very long extremely detailed message.
quests.hint: A good voicemail is brief informative and includes a call-back number.
quests.explanation: A complete professional voicemail includes your name the reason for calling and your number.

quests.scene: You are meeting your partner's parents for the very first time.
options: Say nothing and look at your phone.
Nice to meet you both! I've heard so much about you.
Hello.
Don't worry I'll relax once I know you better.
quests.hint: Make a warm enthusiastic and genuine first impression.
quests.explanation: Nice to meet you both! I've heard so much about you. is warm and engaging.

quests.scene: You need to ask your neighbour to water your plants while you are away travelling.
options: Leave a note on their door.
Hi would you mind watering my plants while I'm away? I'd really appreciate it.
Just leave and hope for the best.
Ask a friend who lives further away.
quests.hint: Ask directly politely and with genuine appreciation.
quests.explanation: Making the request in person with appreciation is more personal and effective than a note.

quests.scene: At a conference you want to speak to a well-known expert. You approach them.
options: You are very famous. I love you!
Excuse me I really enjoyed your talk. May I ask you a question?
Just stand near them and wait.
Hi. Can I talk to you?
quests.hint: Lead with a genuine compliment and then make a specific polite request.
quests.explanation: Complimenting the talk creates a natural positive opening. Asking permission shows respect for their time.

quests.scene: You notice a colleague's presentation contains several factual errors before they present it to the client.
options: Your presentation is full of mistakes.
It's probably fine.
I noticed a few things that might need checking - would you like me to go through them with you?
Say nothing and let them present it incorrectly.
quests.hint: Offer feedback as help and support not as direct criticism.
quests.explanation: Framing your input as helping to check is constructive and kind.

quests.scene: A child is crying loudly in a cafe. The parent looks very stressed and embarrassed.
options: Stare at them.
Ask the staff to remove them.
Smile at the parent warmly and say: It's OK - all kids do this sometimes!
Complain to the manager.
quests.hint: Show empathy and kindness to a stressed parent in a public place.
quests.explanation: A small act of reassurance costs nothing but can significantly comfort a stressed parent.

quests.scene: You need more time to finish a work assignment and must email your manager to explain.
options: I need more time.
I'm making good progress but need a few extra days. Could we extend the deadline to Friday?
The deadline is completely unrealistic.
I'll just submit whatever I have.
quests.hint: Update your manager on your progress AND make a specific reasonable request.
quests.explanation: Updating your manager on progress and asking for a specific deadline is the professional approach.

quests.scene: A cashier gives you too much change by mistake.
options: Keep it - lucky day!
Say nothing and leave quickly.
Excuse me I think you've given me too much change.
Put the extra in the tip jar.
quests.hint: Honesty is always the right choice even when no one would know.
quests.explanation: Pointing out the cashier's mistake is both honest and the morally correct action.

quests.scene: A client has asked for a document by 5pm and you see it is 4:45pm.
options: Send whatever you have without checking it.
I'll send it tomorrow instead.
Please find the document attached. Apologies if it feels slightly rushed - please let me know if anything needs adjustment.
Ignore the email and hope they forget.
quests.hint: Deliver what you can and be transparent about the circumstances.
quests.explanation: Sending the document with a transparent note is professional.

quests.scene: A colleague says: I don't think your idea will work.
options: You're completely wrong.
I appreciate your honesty. Could you tell me why you think that?
Fine forget it then.
Let's take a vote on it.
quests.hint: Use disagreement as an opportunity to learn and improve your idea.
quests.explanation: Asking Why do you think that? turns a challenge into a productive exchange.

quests.scene: A host asks you at a dinner party: Did you enjoy the food?
options: It was OK I suppose.
It was absolutely delicious! Thank you so much for cooking.
I've had better honestly.
Tell me what it was first.
quests.hint: Be generous and sincere with praise when someone has cooked for you.
quests.explanation: It was absolutely delicious! Thank you so much for cooking. is warm and sincere.

quests.scene: You board a crowded bus with heavy bags. Another passenger stands up and offers you their seat.
options: Just take it without saying anything.
I don't need charity.
Oh that's so kind of you! Thank you very much.
No thank you I prefer to stand.
quests.hint: Accept a generous gesture graciously and express genuine gratitude.
quests.explanation: Oh that's so kind of you! Thank you very much. accepts the offer with genuine warmth.

quests.scene: Your child's teacher calls and says: I'm a little concerned about your child's progress in class.
options: They're fine - don't worry about it.
What have they done now?
Thank you for letting me know. Could we arrange a time to discuss this in more detail?
That's your job to fix.
quests.hint: Engage with the teacher as a partner in your child's education.
quests.explanation: Thanking the teacher and asking to meet shows you take their concern seriously.

quests.scene: You accidentally call someone by the wrong name in the middle of a team meeting.
options: Pretend nothing happened.
I'm so incredibly sorry for calling you the wrong name.
Sorry - Sarah I meant.
Just keep going and hope they didn't hear.
quests.hint: A quick light correction is much better than over-apologising or ignoring it.
quests.explanation: A brief natural correction fixes the mistake immediately without drawing more attention to it.

quests.scene: A team meeting ends without clearly assigned next steps. What should you do?
options: Forget about it until the next meeting.
Send a quick follow-up email summarising the agreed actions and owners.
Wait for someone else to send the summary.
Ask someone else to handle the follow-up.
quests.hint: Good professionals proactively follow up after meetings.
quests.explanation: Sending a follow-up summary shows initiative and ensures everyone has clarity on who owns what.

quests.scene: Your doctor recommends a treatment that you feel uncomfortable about.
options: I'm not doing that - end of discussion.
Just do whatever you think is best.
I'm not entirely comfortable with that - could we explore other options together?
Write me a completely different prescription.
quests.hint: Be honest with your doctor about your concerns - this is your right.
quests.explanation: Expressing discomfort and asking about alternatives is assertive and appropriate.
